findings.description: The EBS volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true (and no KMS key is specified), so data written to this additional disk is stored unencrypted.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet (including aws_instance.portal_server) to receive a public IP address, and the subnet is associated with a route table that has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, exposing workloads directly to the internet.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes this a public subnet; combined with the associated route table's default route to the internet gateway, any instance launched here is directly reachable from the internet without an explicit decision.

The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext static credentials. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service and stored unencrypted in the instance attribute, so anyone with instance access or SSRF against 169.254.169.254 obtains long-lived AWS credentials.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device configuration with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled and the hard-coded/role credentials exposed via metadata can be stolen through a simple SSRF against the web server.
Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on an internet-reachable instance to brute-force and exploitation from any source address.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no TLS listener configured, so all portal traffic is transmitted unencrypted and subject to interception or tampering.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted outbound connections that facilitate data exfiltration and command-and-control from a compromised instance.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.

No public access block, bucket ACL, or bucket policy restricting access is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults to prevent public exposure of network metadata.
The bucket has no policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, permitting cleartext access to stored flow logs.

The EBS snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk without any indication of encryption; if the source volume is unencrypted the snapshot stores the portal server's disk contents in cleartext, and snapshots are a common data-exfiltration target if their sharing permissions are ever loosened.

The ENI is created without any security_groups attribute, so it falls back to the VPC default security group rather than the purpose-built aws_security_group.portal_sg. Default security groups are frequently left permissive and are not audited, weakening network segmentation for the interface attached to the portal server.
